account:
Today has mostly followed my appointments: a morning in the office, a plaza market walk, lunch at home, and the afternoon accounts appointment. No correspondence or account figures have been supplied. I tried to ask freight about town trade, but did not get a reply. Townsfolk reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery; that alone seems ordinary.

The tea invitation was initially unclear because the appointment book did not identify the host's cottage. The secretary investigated without finding it, but the neighbour personally confirmed tea at three at the cottage at (16, -60, 105), nearest the east landing. The neighbour said the baker reported no special occasion today. The secretary's earlier calls concerned the missing tea address, so those are explained.

The most notable new business is the builder's request for me to inspect the great hall lighting tomorrow at eighteen hundred. The builder says eight lanterns have been installed and wants my opinion, not money or approval. I agreed and asked the secretary to record it, though the secretary has repeatedly asked for confirmation, so I have not yet verified the entry. The lighting work could simply be an improvement to the hall; I have no evidence of another purpose. I still have a feeling I may be missing something around town, but neither the tea nor the lanterns establishes a hidden gathering or plan.
